unit.title: Databases and SQL for school records

lesson.title: Counts and averages: GROUP BY
lesson.subtitle: Summaries per class, HAVING, and what NULL does

video.title: Counts and averages: GROUP BY
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Every class; A whole Saturday; One query. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The district wants the average science mark for every class, every term. That used to be my whole Saturday, with a calculator. Now it's one query.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: counts and averages for every group, with GROUP BY.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: COUNT: how many rows; AVG: the average; MIN, MAX: lowest, highest; ROUND: fewer decimals.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: SQL can summarise as well as list. COUNT counts rows. AVG gives the average, and MIN and MAX the lowest and highest. And ROUND tidies the decimals.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT class, … Caption: One row per class: how many, and the average
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: On their own, they summarise the whole table into one row. GROUP BY splits the rows into groups, one per class, and summarises each group. So you get one row for every class.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: All the rows; Grouped by class; One row per class.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A group: rows that share a value
scenes.narration: A group is all the rows that share a value, like every row for Six B. Every column you select must be grouped, or summarised.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “WHERE” (Before grouping; Filters rows) and “HAVING” (After grouping; COUNT(*) > 30).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: WHERE filters rows before they're grouped. HAVING filters the groups after: HAVING a count above thirty keeps only the big classes.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Musa missed the science test, so his mark is empty: NULL. When I average the marks, what does AVG do with his?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: AVG skips it: Musa's empty mark is left out, not counted as zero. Counting the mark column skips it too, but COUNT star counts every row. So when the two counts differ, something is missing.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT class, … Caption: 99 out of 20? Find it before you average
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Summaries hide glitches. Before you trust an average, ask for the lowest and highest in each group. A science mark of ninety-nine out of twenty jumps out at once.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Hourly readings; An average per day; Glitches out.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, a week of hourly soil readings becomes one average per day: that's a GROUP BY day. Leave out the glitches, and watch days four and five rise by about three while the median doesn't move.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. After grouping by class, I want only the classes with more than thirty pupils. Which line does that?

scenes.visual: Summary card: COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX; GROUP BY: one row per group; HAVING filters groups; NULLs are skipped. Takeaway bar: One query, one row per group, every term.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: HAVING, because it filters groups after they're counted. Remember: COUNT, AVG, MIN and MAX summarise. GROUP BY makes one row per group. And NULLs are skipped, so check the lowest and highest before you trust an average.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Group by birth month; Each group counts itself; One row per month. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: pupils group themselves by birth month. Each group counts itself, and the class writes one row per month on the board. That's GROUP BY, done with people.

checkpoints.prompt: Musa missed the test, so his mark is NULL. What does AVG(mark) do with it?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — AVG and COUNT(mark) skip NULL; COUNT(*) still counts the row.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — NULL isn't zero. AVG leaves it out, so the average is over the marks that exist.

checkpoints.prompt: After GROUP BY class, which line keeps only classes with more than 30 pupils?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — HAVING filters groups after they're counted; WHERE works on rows before grouping.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — WHERE runs before the groups exist, so it can't use COUNT. HAVING filters the groups.
